label: input c at original position >= 4
explanation: Fires when the input token is the letter c during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase at position t >= 4. On the dev split every such step is active (precision 1.0), and it covers all but 26 tiny activations (about 0% of the mass). Magnitude grows with absolute position: in the examples, c at t=4 is about 0.18 of max, t=5 about 0.46, t=6 about 0.70, and t=8 about 0.97-1.0. This growth is why mass concentrates at longer L. It never fires on c at positions 0-3, on any other input token (only about 2 stray near-zero activations per token), on the <DEL> step, or anywhere in the copy phase, including when c is fed back as an output.

issues: Only minor noise: on the test split, 25 missed activations hold 0.0% of the mass. Almost all are tiny (0.01-0.03 of max) and sit at step 8, the last original token in L=9 sequences, on tokens other than c. One miss was a c at t=7 (0.73) shown in the context window. The real miss was a 0.02 activation on y at step 8. This is scattered noise, not a systematic class.

Profile confirms the claims. Zero activation at t=0-3, in the delimiter phase and in the copy phase (including recall_idx >= 0). In_tok c holds 100% of the mass. The other tokens have 2 activations each.

The magnitude claim is consistent with the mass shares per active step: t=4 has 0.124 of the mass over 13820 actives, while t=8 has 0.118 over only 2713. So per-step magnitude grows with position. The explanation's numbers come from examples and are approximate.
Test scores: precision 1.0, recall 0.9994, F1 0.9997, mass recall 0.99998. There are no false positives.
